script:
Presenter: Why was this project started?
Salma: We wanted to make electricity-saving classroom sensor because our school community needed a practical improvement.
Presenter: Where did you plan the first version?
Salma: We began in the science laboratory, where our teacher organised responsibilities for everyone.
Presenter: When was the team meeting held?
Salma: It was Wednesday afternoon, which allowed our team to prepare without missing lessons.
Presenter: Which item was particularly useful?
Salma: We used a movement sensor, and checked that it was suitable for the task.
Presenter: Who checked the details and safety?
Salma: We consulted the school engineer instead of trusting rumours or making unsupported claims.
Presenter: Did students work completely alone?
Salma: No, our teacher supervised carefully, while students researched information and shared different responsibilities.
Presenter: What problem appeared during the project?
Salma: Our first attempt contained unreliable movement detection, so the results needed further checking.
Presenter: How did your group correct the error?
Salma: We returned to repeated testing results and explained our correction clearly to teammates.
Presenter: Who will benefit from your work?
Salma: We hope teachers and students will gain useful information from the finished project.
Presenter: What did users suggest improving?
Salma: They recommended a manual switch, and we recorded their suggestions for the next version.
Presenter: How did you handle disagreements?
Salma: We listened respectfully, considered the evidence and tested the strongest suggestions together.
Presenter: What did the team do with feedback?
Salma: We discussed comments at our weekly meeting and made a clear improvement plan.
Presenter: What will you prepare next term?
Salma: Our next step will be a solar-power project, building on the experience gained this term.
Presenter: What is the most important lesson?
Salma: We learned the value of safe and evidence-based invention, honest feedback and careful preparation. Every group member also checked the final explanation and asked useful questions before sharing it with others.
